critical_finding: Two independent methods improve the legal/language purity ratio by ~20%: (1) language-center projection reduces language purity from 0.975 to 0.684 while maintaining legal purity at 0.295, and (2) Erwägungen-only TF-IDF achieves the highest absolute legal purity (0.385) by focusing on legal reasoning text. However, no method achieves the target ratio >1.0 (legal purity exceeding language purity). The fundamental challenge remains: the primary geometric signal in the BGer corpus is language, not legal content.
notes: Cycle 33021595718 tested three approaches to the language dominance problem: (1) linear projection to remove language-correlated embedding directions, (2) citation-graph node2vec embeddings, and (3) section-specific TF-IDF. Language projection improves the ratio by 20% but reduces absolute legal purity. Citation graph has too low coverage (5%) to meaningfully affect the 1000-decision map. Reasoning-only TF-IDF achieves the best absolute legal purity by focusing on legally substantive text. ORCHESTRATION DIAGNOSIS: Run 33021595718 introduced a scope violation by modifying .opencode/agents/* (adding external_directory permissions for /tmp/lex_*). This was diagnosed as the same class of violation as run 33020332703, reverted, and documented. The permission changes are operationally necessary for experiments to access the control plane but must be made at the workflow level, not by individual lane runs. A minor bug in citation_embeddings.py (node2vec library path returns Word2Vec model instead of (matrix, vocab) tuple) was fixed in this repair cycle. The sachverhalt_erwaegungen legal_purity discrepancy (0.344 in unified evaluation vs 0.377 in individual experiment) is explained by the unified evaluation restricting to 857 decisions with extractable reasoning sections for fair cross-method comparison.
